section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: ADMISSION TO EXAMINATIONS
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Registration by a student for a specific academic term (semester, year or block) also constitutes
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: registration for examinations, subject to all the applicable rules.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: No examination can be written when the student is not formally registered.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: A student’s registration does not include such a student’s application to write a special examination.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: All examinations shall be conducted at a venue determined by TUT, and students shall take exami-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: nations at the venue determined for the campus where he or she is registered.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Only registered students of TUT may sit for examinations at the University.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: A student shall not be admitted to an examination in a module/subject with its own alpha-numerical
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: code, consisting of seven characters, if he or she has not been officially registered for that module/
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: subject and has not obtained the required predicate mark of at least 40%.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: In cases where laboratory work and/or practical  assignments form part of a module/subject, the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: marks obtained for such work shall be taken into account for admission to the examination.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: In the case of Arts and Performing Arts projects, the accumulated total of a project should be at
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: least 40% before a student may submit work for final assessment. If the required 40% has not been
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: obtained, the student may not submit work for final assessment, and he or she will have to repeat
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the assessment.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.3.9  On re-registration for a module/subject, any predicate mark or practical mark previously obtained
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: for that module/subject shall lapse, unless clearly specified in a different way in the Prospectus and
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the study guide.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.3.10  A student who has been expelled from TUT, and who is not, as a result of such expulsion, allowed
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: on the campus of the University, shall not be allowed to take or sit for any examination.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.3.11  A student whose class and/or residence fees have not been paid in full, or who has any other TUT
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: debts, may take or sit for an examination, but his or her results shall not be published before the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: full outstanding amount is settled. Such a student shall, however, be informed if he or she qualifies
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: for a supplementary examination.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: PREDICATE/FULL PERIOD MARK
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: The University has an official predicate day, at least five (5) working days before the classes of-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: ficially end, on which these marks will be announced. Particulars of predicate day are published in
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the Important Dates for the Academic Year in front of this Part of the Prospectus.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Students shall be allowed only five (5) working days after the official publication of the predicate/full
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: period marks to appeal to the Head of the Department, relevant lecturer or staff member concerned,
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: if they are of the opinion that their published marks are incorrect. The Head of the Department,
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: relevant lecturer or designated staff member should adjust the marks within the five-day period and
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: issue the student with proof that the department acknowledged the change in marks.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: All students assume full responsibility for checking their marks. After publication of the results, re-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: quests for adjustments of predicate/full period marks will only be allowed in exceptional cases and
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: must be approved by the respective Executive Dean on request of the module/subject lecturer (via
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the Head of the Department).  The Registrar’s Environment must amend all records, and students
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: must be provided with the amended results.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Students' Rules and Regulations
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: be published on the notice boards of the service points for distance education students.

text: 4.1.5.1  Main examinations
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (a)  Only modules/subjects in which a student has examination admission will be listed  on the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: student’s personal examination timetable.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (b)  Only the examination timetables posted on the official notice boards at the different campuses;
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: and the personal timetables issued to students by the Registrar's Environment are considered
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: to be the official examination timetable of the University. The Distance Education Unit will post
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the individual student timetable to students at least six (6) weeks in advance and publish them
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: on the University's website and myTUTor. The University will not be held liable for a lost, late
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: or undelivered individual student timetable. The University will not  accept responsibility for
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: incorrect information concerning examination arrangements provided by unauthorised persons.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: It is the responsibility of the student to ensure that the information reflecting on his or her
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: timetable is correct.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (d)  The final official examination timetable shall be available approximately four (4) weeks before
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the commencement of examinations. Student’s personal examination timetables can be col-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: lected during predicate week.

text: (e)  Staff  members  are  not  authorized  to  furnish  the  main  examination  timetables  information
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: telephonically to students by telephone. Students may, however, view the official examination
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: timetable on the University’s website www.tut.ac.za or faculty dedicated notice boards.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: The examination venue, date and session of each question paper shall be printed next to the

text: subject and predicate mark on each student’s personal timetable.

section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: www.tut.ac.za by means of the publication schedule. Not applicable to distance education
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: students.

text: (b)  Students should collect their personal supplementary examination timetables at the exami-

section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the University’s website, www.tut.ac.za by means of the publication schedule. Not applicable
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: to distance education students.

text: Only the examination timetables posted on the official notice boards at the different campuses;

text: and the personal timetables issued to students by the Registrar’s Environment are considered

text: to be the official examination timetable of the University.

text: Special examinations
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (a)  A special  examination shall not be valid unless the student’s registration for the  academic
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: year or semester concerned have been approved.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (b)  Special Examination one  (1)  maybe granted to  a student who was unable to write  a  main
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: exam, as a result of illness or as a result of extenuating circumstances, subject to the approval
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: of the Registrar or his/her designate.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (c)  A student who qualifies for a special examination (special examination one (1)) and have a
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: valid reason to miss the special examination (special examination one (1)) as a result of illness,
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: or as a result of extenuating circumstances, may apply to write special examination two (2).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (d)  A student who qualifies for the main examination but have a valid reason to be absent from
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the main examination and special examination one (1), as a result of extended illness or due
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: to the later publication of results, may apply to write special examination two (2), or where
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: applicable an exit examination. This will be the student’s final opportunity.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: In the case of distance education, examinations will take place during the main examinations/
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: supplementary examinations.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Exit examinations
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (a)  Prior to the application of an exit  examination, a student’s registration for the qualification
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: should not have been interrupted.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (b)  The student should have been registered for the module/subject, obtained a predicate mark
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: and write an examination during the period of registration.  The necessary minimum admission
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: requirements to the main examination shall also apply to the exit exam.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (c)  The student must take the examination on the campus where he/she has been registered for
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the subject concerned.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (d)  All students who remained with one subject to qualify for their respective qualifications, regard-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: less of whether they have already had two opportunities to write an examination in a specific
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: subject, in a particular study period – including students who remained with one continuous
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: assessment subject to qualify for their respective qualifications, will be allowed to apply for
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: exit examinations.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (e)  The student must submit an application to write an exit examination to the Registrar’s Environ-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: ment before the closing date published in the University Core Calendar.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (f)  A student who, for any reason whatsoever, does not write an exit examination, will fail the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: module(s) concerned, and not further examination opportunity shall be granted.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: If a student fails the exit examination, he/she must register for the module/subject and obtain
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: a new predicate mark.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (h)  Students who have been  granted  permission to take exit examinations should collect their
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: examination timetables at the examination counters of the respective campuses at least one
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (1) day before the commencement of the applicable examination period, as published in the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: University’s academic calendar.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: In the case of distance education, examinations will take place during the main examinations/
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: supplementary examinations.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Coinciding of examinations on timetables (timetable clashes)
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (a)  TUT shall assume no responsibility for the coinciding, on any timetable, of examinations of
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: modules/subjects due to students’ repeating of modules/subjects, although students will be
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: accommodated as far as possible.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Students' Rules and Regulations
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (b)  The University shall not accommodate cases where examination times or dates coincide as
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: a result of a simultaneous registration for another qualification, registration at another tertiary
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: institution, or as a result of responsibilities placed on a student by, for example, an employer.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: The student shall  notify  the  Registrar's Environment at the campus  concerned or,  in
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the case of distance education, the distance education examination office, about the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: coinciding examination dates. He or she has to complete the required form in writing at
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: least ten (10) working days before the examination date concerned, and, in the case of
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: distance education, at least four (4) weeks prior to the commencement of examinations.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Enquiries regarding the venue arrangements made to accommodate the coinciding of
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: examinations should be made at the Registrar's Environment  early the morning (08:00)
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: before the examinations of the modules/subjects concerned are to be written.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Both modules/subjects concerned shall be written on the same day, although at different
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: examination sessions.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Cases of coinciding examinations shall be accommodated in a separate examination
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: venue, where students shall be kept under constant invigilation.

text: TUT shall assume no responsibility for incorrect information on examination arrangements, as given
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: by unauthorised persons.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: The date and time determined for an examination should be carefully observed and adhered to.

["CHAPTER 4"]

text: nation session commences.

["CHAPTER 4"]

text: hand in their personal belongings.

section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.6.11  Students should carefully read the instructions on the question papers and the back pages of the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: examination scripts, and should comply with those instructions.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.6.12  All written test and examination answers should be written in black or blue ink.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Students' Rules and Regulations
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.6.13  Students  should  ensure  that  their  student  numbers  and  names  are  written  down  correctly,  as
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: requested on the examination scripts and attendance slips.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.6.14  No explanations of examination questions may be requested or provided.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.6.15  A student should indicate to the invigilator that he or she is ready to hand in his or her examination
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: material by remaining seated and raising a hand. An invigilator shall collect the examination material
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: from the student at his or her seat.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.6.16  As soon as a student has handed in his or her work, he or she should leave the examination venue.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: No student shall be allowed to leave the examination venue before at least thirty (30) minutes have
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: lapsed after the examination has commenced.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.6.17  All examination rules shall apply, with the necessary changes, to all tests.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Please note that rules 4.1.6.19 to 4.1.6.26 herein shall apply during examinations and tests, and
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: a student shall commit an irregularity if he or she does not adhere to those rules.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.6.18  While an examination is in progress, no student may help or try to help another student obtain as-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: sistance or attempt to obtain assistance, or communicate or try to communicate with any person
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: other than the person who has officially been authorised thereto by the Registrar.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.6.19  Unless stipulated otherwise for an examination, students may not have the following in their pos-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: session while they are in the examination venue, with the exception of their personal examination
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: timetables and whatever is handed to them in the examination venue:
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (a)  any blank, unused paper;
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (b)  any book, memorandum, note, sketch, map, film or any other document;
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (c)  any other aid that has a bearing on the examination modules/subjects, even if it bears no
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: relation to the examination itself;
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (d)  any phones, or smart watches, even if they are switched off – if a student is found in posses-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: sion of a phone or smart watch, disciplinary steps shall be taken against him or her;
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (e)  earphones or any other electronic devices; and
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: pencil bags, pencil cases or any other bags or containers.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.6.20  The rules on  open-book  examinations allow students to be in  possession of additional material
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: required by the assessor.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.6.21  A student may not use a pocket calculator in an examination unless expressly authorised to do so
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: in the instructions appearing on the question paper concerned, and then only those pocket calcula-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: tors that are specifically permitted. The calculator facility of a cellular telephone may not be used
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: as such during examinations.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.6.22  A student may not disregard any examination instruction given by the invigilator.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.6.23  Students are not permitted to have or make notes, or to do calculations on their question papers,
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: personal timetables, stationery or any other object. Rough work may be done on the examination
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: script. If any part of such work should not be marked, a line should be drawn through it.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.6.24  All examination scripts and aids handed out to students should be handed in again before the stu-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: dents leave the examination venue. Unless otherwise stipulated, students may take their question
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: papers with them when they leave. All question papers printed on coloured paper should be handed
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: in.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Students' Rules and Regulations
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.6.25  A student may not cause a disturbance in an examination venue or conduct himself or herself in
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: an improper or unseemly manner.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.6.26  A student may not have any firearm in his or her possession while he or she is in the examination
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: venue (see Chapter 19).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: CIRCUMSTANTIAL  REASSESSMENT
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Although TUT deals with care and responsibility with the receipt, distribution and  safekeeping of
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: examination  scripts,  documents  or  objects  for  practical  examinations,  disks  or  micro-disks,  as
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: well as portfolios, reports, scripts, dissertations and theses, the University does not assume any
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: responsibility for such examination material being lost, stolen or destroyed. In case that happens,
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the University reserves the right to request a student to be re-assessed.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: If there should be any doubt about the validity of the circumstances under which a student took an
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: examination, the University reserves the right to request that student to be re-assessed.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: EXAMINATION ARRANGEMENTS FOR STUDENTS WITH PHYSICAL DISABILITIES
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Objective
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: The objective is to accommodate students with disabilities (as defined in the Policy on Students
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: with Disabilities), whether permanent or temporary, by means of additional arrangements, which
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: may include –
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: additional time;
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: furnishing question papers in Braille or large print;
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: oral examinations;
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: special equipment (computers, where appropriate); and
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: special or separate venues and invigilators.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Procedure
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (a)  Application for disability classification  must be submitted to the Directorate of Student De-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: velopment and Support, who identifies and evaluates students with permanent or temporary
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: disabilities, when they apply for special arrangements.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (b)  The Directorate of Student Development and Support formally notifies the Registrar’s Environ-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: ment of any recommendation, where upon that section makes the necessary arrangements.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (c)  Students with temporary disabilities (injuries, temporary impediments or disorders) apply at
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the  Registrar’s  Environment,  furnishing  substantiation  for  (proof  of)  such  disability.  Regis-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: trar’s Environment will refer the application to the Directorate of Student Development and
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Support, for recommendation and/or verification.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (d)  The student administrator scrutinises recommendations, as verified or formulated by the Di-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: rectorate for Student Development and Support, and determines what special arrangements
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: should be made.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (e)  Registrar’s Environment arranges the examination event (venue, invigilator, question paper,
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: etc.) and duly informs the student.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: EXAMINATION AND TEST IRREGULARITIES OR MISCONDUCT
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: A student commits an examination irregularity when he or she does not adhere to the rules set out
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: All examination rules and instructions shall apply, with the necessary changes, to all tests, con-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: tinuous assessments, block-based offerings and all off-campus examinations and tests.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Students' Rules and Regulations
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Irregularities should immediately be brought to the attention of the relevant Assistant Registrar of
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the specific campus, in writing. The latter shall report the matter to the Head of Student Discipli-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: nary Services, who shall, after giving the student an opportunity to put his or her case in a written
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: statement, submit a report, accompanied by the necessary evidence, to the academic disciplinary
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: committee concerned.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: POWERS OF INVIGILATORS
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.10.1  An invigilator may confiscate the examination documents of any student or any prohibited aid or
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: material found in the possession of any student, during the examination, if the invigilator suspects
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: that an irregularity has taken place.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.10.2  When an irregularity is suspected, the student concerned shall hand over the examination script or
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: scripts that he or she has used up to that point, at the request of the invigilator.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.10.3  The student will then be instructed to continue with the examination and he/she will be given a new
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: examination script.  Once again, the invigilator will indicate on the new script the exact time the script
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: was handed to him/her.  No additional time will be allocated to the student.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.10.4  A student may not claim that the opportunity to continue with the examination is a condonation of
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: his/her alleged infraction of the rules.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: DISCIPLINARY MEASURES
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.11.1  Misconduct
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Any student who contravenes an examination rule is guilty of misconduct and shall be dealt with
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: in terms of the Disciplinary Code for Students (see Chapter 15). Cases of misconduct shall be the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: following:
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Intentionally or negligently contravening or subverting, or attempting to contravene or subvert,
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: or assisting, encouraging or persuading any another person to contravene or subvert a code,
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: regulation (15.1.3).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (b)  Refusal to obey any fair or reasonable instruction or request of any statutory body,  lecturer,
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: member of the Students’ Representative Council, any official or any person acting on behalf
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: of the University, or any violation of such instruction or request within the framework of any
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: rule, regulation or law applicable to the University (15.1.4).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (c)  Damaging, defacing, destruction, theft, housebreaking and theft, appropriation or alienation of
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: University property or property controlled by the University, including that of another student,
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: employee, visitor or person associated with the University, or any attempt to do so (15.1.5).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Improper, disgraceful or indecent behaviour on any premises of the University or premises
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: controlled by the University or at any other place where the student’s behaviour is identifiable
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: with or can possibly be identified with the University (15.1.9).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (e)  Any abusive, swearing or indecent act towards any employee, student or person associated
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: with the University that is a violation of his or her dignity or body, either on the premises of
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the University or elsewhere (15.1.10).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (f)  Engaging in behaviour that may bring the image of the University into disrepute, or any act
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: that may be detrimental to or jeopardise the maintenance of discipline, or which is detrimental
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: to providing normal services, efficient tuition and the conducting of research (15.1.11).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (g)  Using  violence  against,  or  threatening,  or  intimidating  any  person  on  any  premises  of  the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: University or premises controlled by the University, or during participating in any University
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: activity, or anywhere else where the student may be identified with the University (15.1.12).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Students' Rules and Regulations
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (h)  Helping or trying to help another student during a class test, examination or any form of assess-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: ment, or obtaining or trying to obtain help from another student during such test, examination
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: or assessment, or the submission of any test, examination script or written assignment or any
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: assessment of another student in his or her name (15.1.14).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (i)  Being in possession of any form of unauthorised notes, using or trying to use notes that have
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: relevance, or any kind of resource during any test or examination, except where the supervi-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: sor or lecturer concerned has consented explicitly to such possession and/or use, or refusal
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: to hand over such notes to the invigilator, or destroying or trying to destroy such notes in any
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: way, or making notes during a test or examination on any object, ruler or pocket calculator,
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: except as laid down and permitted (15.1.15).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (j)  Handing in any written assignment for assessment in which the essential parts of the assess-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: ment have been copied from the work of another person, or any form of plagiarism (15.1.16).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (k)  Making  a  deliberately  false  statement  or  furnishing  false  information  to  any  University
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: employee,  official  body,  committee,  any  person  associated  with  the  University,  Students’
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Representative Council or any student who is a student leader (15.1.18).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Forging any certificate, degree, diploma, document or statement of the University, or submit-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: ting any forged document to the University (15.1.20).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (m)  Using the student card of another student or an access card of another person or allowing
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: another student or any person to use such a student card or access card to perform any action
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: or obtain any benefit or service that can be performed or obtained with such a card (15.1.23).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (n)  Encouraging or inciting a fellow student or another person, or conspiring with another person
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: to contravene any of the rules of the University (15.1.29).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (o)  Failing to report the misconduct of another student of which he or she is aware, or that he or
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: she has witnessed (15.1.30).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.11.2  Academic Disciplinary Committee
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (a)  The Academic Disciplinary Committee comprises the following members (15.4.1):
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: A chairperson designated by the Vice-Chancellor.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: The head of the academic department concerned or his or her proxy.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: An employee designated by the Registrar.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: A representative of the Students’ Representative Council concerned, as designated by
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the Students’ Representative Council.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (b)  Three (3) members shall constitute a quorum (15.4.2).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (c)  The chairperson may co-opt an employee with a legal background to be a member of the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Academic Disciplinary Committee (15.4.3).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (d)  The Academic Disciplinary Committee shall keep a register of all disciplinary decisions made
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: and measures taken (15.4.4).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (e)  The functions of the Academic Disciplinary Committee shall be as follows (15.4.5):
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: To hear all cases of alleged misconduct taking place during normal academic activities.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: To hear all cases of alleged misconduct in academic affairs relating to the classroom.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: To hear all cases of alleged misconduct in academic affairs relating to tests or examina-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: tion activities.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (f)  The Academic Disciplinary Committee shall report to the Senate on its disciplinary decisions
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: and measures (15.4.6).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Students' Rules and Regulations
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.11.3  Disciplinary measures
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: The Academic Disciplinary Committee may take one or more of the following disciplinary measures
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: or impose any of the following sanctions (rules 15.12.1(a) – (r)):
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Issue a reprimand.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Issue a warning.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Imposing a suspended disciplinary measure or suspending a portion thereof or suspending
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the imposition of a disciplinary measure on such conditions, as it deems appropriate.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Imposing expulsion.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (e)  Excluding a student from any or all lectures, tests or examinations in any or all modules/
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: subjects.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (f)  Cancelling any module/subject, test, examination or other marks, as well as year and semester
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: marks.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (g)  Cancelling credits in any or all modules/subjects.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (h)  Refusing to issue a certificate.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (i)  Recommending to the Senate to cancel a qualification that has been formally awarded or
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: conferred.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (j)  Excluding a student from any or all classrooms, test or examination rooms.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (k)  Excluding a student from any or all academic activities.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (l)  Discharging the student from any office or capacity in which he or she was appointed or to
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: which he or she was elected.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Instructing the student to apologise, verbally or in writing, to any person or body in a manner
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: determined by the Academic Disciplinary Committee.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Imposing the forfeiture of a bursary or loan.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (o)  Referring the student to the Bureau for Academic Support for suitable remedial measures.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (p)  Taking any other appropriate, educationally justifiable disciplinary measure, to be confirmed
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: by the Disciplinary Committee.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Imposing the forfeiture of any right or privilege the student is entitled to as a registered student.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (r)  Sending a letter confirming the finding, as well as the disciplinary measures imposed by the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Academic Disciplinary Committee, to the parent, guardian or employer of the student.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: PASS REQUIREMENTS
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.12.1  A student shall pass a module/subject by obtaining a final mark of 50% or more for that module/
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: subject, subject to  rules 4.1.3.6  and  4.1.9, and  by obtaining a final  mark of  50% or more for  a
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: module/subject with its own alpha-numerical code, consisting of seven (7) characters, subject to
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: rule 4.1.3.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: In addition to the final mark of 50%, a student should obtain a subminimum mark of at least 40% in
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: a theoretical examination in order to pass, and where the examination in a module/subject consists
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: of two (2) or more question papers, he or she should obtain a subminimum mark of at least 40%
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: for each paper.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Students' Rules and Regulations
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: In addition to the final mark of 50%, a student should obtain a subminimum mark of at least 50%
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: practical examination module/subject.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: In modules/subjects where students take formal examinations, the final mark shall be calculated by
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: combining the predicate mark and the examination mark at a 50:50 ratio. Deviating ratios, approved
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: by Senate.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.12.5  The decision of the University in respect of practical work and projects that contribute to the calcula-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: tion of the examination mark shall be final and no student’s work shall be re-marked.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.12.6  The final mark for non-terminating modules/subjects shall be compiled from the accumulation of
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: marks obtained for tests, assignments, papers, projects and other opportunities. An accumulated
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: pass mark of 50% is required in these modules/subjects.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.12.7  A student shall pass a module/subject with distinction by obtaining a final mark of 75% or more in
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: that module/subject. This implies that the student should obtain an average mark of at least 75%
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: for the related modules (see Chapter 9 in respect of qualifications obtained cum laude).
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.12.8  Failed modules/subjects shall not be condoned. If a student is allowed to register for the next level,
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: year  or  semester,  it  does  not  imply  that  the  failed  modules/subjects  have  been  condoned.  The
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: student should re-register for and pass the failed modules/subjects.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.12.9  A student may be promoted to a subsequent year or semester, subject to the provisions contained
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: in Chapter 2.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.12.10  Modules/subjects  taken  and  passed  for  non-degree  purposes  may  be  applied  for  obtaining  a
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: qualification: provided that all admission and accreditation requirements are met.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.12.11  Credit can be withdrawn for a module/subject in which the examination of it's prerequisite module/
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: subject has not been passed.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Minimum pass requirements

text: A final pass mark of 50% is required to pass an exit examination and
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the relevant minimum rule applies.

text: Practical assessment
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: modules/subjects
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: A minimum of 50% in the examination is required to pass.

text: Practical examination

text: modules/subjects

text: A final pass mark of 50% is required to pass, and a minimum of 50%

text: in the examination is required to pass.

text: examination modules/

text: subjects

text: A final pass mark of 50% is required to pass, and a minimum of 50% for

text: more than one question papers, the student shall obtain a minimum of

text: 40% for each of the papers, respectively.

text: A final pass mark of 50% is required to pass a supplementary exami-

text: nation and the relevant minimum rule applies.

text: A final pass mark of 50% is required to pass a supplementary examina-

text: tion and the relevant minimum rule applies. No further opportunities will
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: be granted if a student forfeits or fails the supplementary examination.

text: PUBLICATION OF RESULTS
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.13.1  Staff members may not furnish examination results by telephone. Students may, however, obtain
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the examination results on the University’s website at: www.tut.ac.za.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: In the case of distance education students, the examination results will be mailed to students by the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Distance Education Unit and will be the only official examination results given to distance education
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: students. However, the University assumes no liability for delays in the mail, or for mail that was
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: not delivered or not received.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.13.2  Statements of examination credits obtained, examination results and academic records shall be
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: valid only if they are printed on the approved forms and issued by the Registrar.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.13.3  The examination results of a student with any outstanding fees and/or library material shall not be
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: made known or published before the outstanding amount has been paid in full or the library material
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: has been returned. However, such a student shall be informed of admission to and particulars of a
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: supplementary examination, if applicable.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: SUPPLEMENTARY EXAMINATIONS
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.14.1  A supplementary examination shall take place directly after the main examination.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.14.2  The predicate mark obtained for admission to the main examination shall also apply to the sup-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: plementary examination.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.14.3  A student who fails the main examination in a module/subject, but obtains a final mark of at least
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 45%, qualifies for a supplementary examination. A student who obtains a final mark of 50% but
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: failed the minimum subminimum also qualifies for a supplementary examination.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.14.4  A student who fails one (1) or more question paper(s) in the main examination, but who qualifies
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: for a supplementary examination in terms of rule 4.1.14.3, retains credit for the question paper or
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: papers that he or she has passed in the main examination, and takes a supplementary examina-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: tion on the question paper(s) he or she has failed. A module/subject should be passed in the main
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: examination or the subsequent supplementary examination.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.14.5  A supplementary examination shall be conducted and its marks calculated in the same manner as
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: that of the main examination.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.14.6  Students who qualify for supplementary examinations will be published on the University website
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: www.tut.ac.za  according to the  daily  publication schedule.  Not  applicable to  distance  education
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: students.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: It is each student’s own responsibility to consult the University website to find out whether he or she
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: qualifies for a supplementary examination. The individual results of distance education students will
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: show them whether they qualify for supplementary examinations. Distance education students who
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: qualify for supplementary examinations will have an opportunity to participate during the consecutive
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: examination period, i.e. students who qualify for supplementary examinations in May will have to
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: take their supplementary examinations in October/November and vice versa.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: In the event that a student qualifies for an exit examination after a supplementary examination period
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: due to late publication, such a student must wait for the next examination opportunity to write the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: examination.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.14.9  No supplementary examination opportunities will be granted in modules/subjects that are assessed
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: in a non-examination terminating mode.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.14.10  A student who does not take or does not complete a supplementary examination for any reason
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: whatsoever, shall fail the relevant module/subject. Only one (1) opportunity to take a supplementary
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: examination shall be granted for a specific module/subject per academic period.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.14.11  The  requirements  for  supplementary  examinations  for  modules/subjects  that  are  continuously
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: assessed are given in rule 4.1.17.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Students' Rules and Regulations
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.14.12  No supplementary examination shall be granted on the basis of marks obtained in a special exami-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: nation.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.14.13  If a student applies for a re-marking or re-checking, it does not imply that he or she may take a
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: supplementary examination. Permission to take a supplementary examination shall be granted after
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: re-marking or re-checking only if the student qualifies for it according to rule 4.1.14.3.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.14.14  If a student fails the supplementary examination, he or she has to re-register for the module/subject.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Distance education students must submit new assignments after their re-registration for modules/
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: subjects.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.14.15  Distance education students will be granted supplementary examinations in terms of rule 4.1.14.3.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: SPECIAL EXAMINATIONS
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (a)  Special  examinations  shall  be  conducted,  if  possible,  at  the  same  time  as  supplementary
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: examinations or exit examinations. The predicate mark obtained for admission to the main
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: examination shall also apply to special examinations. Distance education students: refer to
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (b)  A special examination may be granted, subject to the approval of the Registrar or his or her
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: designate to a student who was prevented from preparing for the main examination, or who
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: was prevented from writing the main examination during an examination period, as a result
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: of illness, or as a result of circumstances beyond his or her control (e.g. technology failure in
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: computer-based assessment).  Distance education students: refer to rule 4.1.14.7.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: If a student has been prevented from writing one or more question paper(s) in a module/subject
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: consisting of more than one (1) question paper(s), the student may take a special examination
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: only in the question paper(s) concerned. The student shall retain the marks for the question
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: paper(s) written during the main examination.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: If a student has a valid reason to miss the supplementary examination, he/she may submit an
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: application at the Registrar’s Environment to write an Special examination before the closing
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: date published in the Academic Core Calendar of the University.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (e)  A student shall not take a special examination in cases where he or she –
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: did not read the examination timetable correctly;
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: did not arrive in time for a particular examination session, or did not arrive for it at all.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: reacted to unofficial information; or
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: was prevented from writing.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (f)  A student may, notwithstanding the provisions above, submit a written appeal to the Regis-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: trar’s Environment for consideration, if such a student is of the opinion that his or her case
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: has merit that should be taken into consideration. This appeal is required to be submitted
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: to  the  Registrar’s  Environment  within  three  (3)  days  of  the  date  of  the  examination  the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: student had been unable to write on account of the specific circumstances. On payment of
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the prescribed fee, the application will be submitted to the Registrar for consideration.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (g)  An  application  to  take  special  examination  in  terms  of  rules  4.1.15(c)  should  be  submit-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: ted  to  the  Registrar’s  Environment  on  the  required  form,  accompanied  by  all  the  support-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: ing  evidence,  as  well  as  proof  of  payment  of  the  fixed  fee  for  the  special  circumstances
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: special  examination,  within  three  (3)  working  days  of  the  date  of  the  examination  that
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the  student  has  failed  to  take  on  account  of  the  unavoidable  special  circumstances.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (h)  Special examinations shall be conducted and their marks calculated in the same manner as
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: those of the main examinations.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (i)  A student who fails the special examination will only be granted a second opportunity under
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: special circumstances as approved by the Registrar.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Students' Rules and Regulations
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (j)  A student, who, for any reason whatsoever, does not take the special examination, shall fail
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the subject(s)/module(s) concerned, and no further examination opportunity shall be granted.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: EXIT EXAMINATION
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: All students who remain with one (1) subject to qualify for their respective qualifications, regard-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: less of whether they have already had two (2) opportunities to write and examination in a specific
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: subject, in a particular study period – including students with one continuous assessment subject
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: to qualify for the respective qualification, will be allowed to apply for Exit examinations.  This rule
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: applies to NATED as well as HEQSF-aligned qualifications.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: A student shall not be allowed a third opportunity to take an examination in a module/subject
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: in a particular study period, whatever the reason may be and whether the student had made
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: use of each opportunity or not.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: In order to qualify for an exit examination, a student’s registration should not have been inter-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: rupted.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: In the case of distance education students, exit examinations shall be conducted during the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: next examination period.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.16.1  A student may take an exit examination on the following conditions:
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: If it is the only remaining theoretical/continuous module/subject the student needs to pass in
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: order to qualify for the qualification;
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: If  a  student  was  registered  for  that  module/subject,  in  the  case  of  a  year  module/subject,
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: during the preceding study period, and, in the case of a semester module/subject, during the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: preceding two study periods;
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: If the student obtained a predicate of at least 40% in that module/subject;
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: If the student did not interrupt his or her registration; and
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: If  the  student  wrote  the  examination  at  the  campus  where  he  or  she  is  registered  for  the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: module/subject concerned.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.16.2  Heads of academic departments could, in exceptional cases, on a discretionally basis approve an
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: exit examination in a non-theoretical module/subject, on condition that such ruling is not explicitly
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: excluded by the rules for the specific module/subject.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: If a student fails the exit examination, he or she must register for the module/subject and obtain a
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: new predicate mark.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.16.4  An exit examination will be conducted and calculated in the same format as the main examination.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.16.5  An application to write an exit examination is required to be submitted to Registrar's Environment
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: before the closing date published with the examination results.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: NON-EXAMINATION TERMINATING MODEL
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.17.1  Academic  departments  may  determine  the  required  number  of  assessments  contributing  to  the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: final mark, but not less than four per semester module/subject and six for a year subject. Specifi-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: cations of the required number of assessments should be published in the relevant study guides
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: or programme handbook especially in the modular modules/subjects.  This contributes to the final
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: pass or promotion mark, expressed as a final percentage.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.17.2  A single assessment opportunity may not contribute more than 40% to the final mark for the module/
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: subject. Where only two (2) assessment opportunities apply, one of which is a practical assessment,
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the practical assessment shall contribute 60% to the final mark.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.17.3  The head of the academic department may determine the subminimum requirements for individual
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: assessment opportunities.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.17.4  A student shall be successful when the accumulated total of all the assessments equals or exceeds
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 50%. He or she will obtain a distinction when the accumulated total equals or exceeds 75%.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Students' Rules and Regulations
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.17.5  An accumulated total of less than 50% indicates that the student fails the module/subject and has
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: to repeat it.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.17.6  No supplementary examination or re-mark shall be granted. Special assessments under special
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: circumstances may  be  granted by  the  Head  of the Department, where the  student forfeited  the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: normal opportunities for appraisal, on submission of the necessary substantiation by the student.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.17.7  The granting of reassessments is not obligatory. A reassessment opportunity may, however, be
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: given to a student who failed a particular assessment opportunity, but attained a minimum mark of
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: between 45% and 48%. Such opportunity follows directly after the failed opportunity.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Please note that the above stipulation shall apply only if it forms part of an individual academic
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: departmental policy and is published as such in the relevant study guide.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.17.8  The same careful assessment and moderation of the first opportunity shall apply to the additional
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: opportunity.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.17.9  Please note that in contrast to modules/subjects that follow the formative assessment examination
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: continuum, where  supplementary examinations  are  scheduled for students  who  have  adequate
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: admission marks, but who failed to obtain the subminimum in the examination, continuous assess-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: ment shall not provide for any summative reassessment, either before or after the adding up of the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: final promotion mark.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.17.10  The head of the academic department may grant a special assessment, under exceptional circum-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: stances, when a student has forfeited the normal opportunities for appraisal and submits the neces-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: sary substantiation for that.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.17.11  The examination rules of TUT shall apply to the placement of students, the procedures followed in
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the assessment venue, and the invigilation during such assessments.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.17.12  Students  have an opportunity to give inputs on their  final  marks before the  final  entering of the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: marks on the electronic database if their calculations differ from those of the relevant lecturer.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.17.13  Marks for individual assessment opportunities shall be made known by the academic department
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: concerned after assessment and moderation.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.17.14  Marks for every assessment opportunity, as well as the final mark, shall be checked and verified
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: before publication.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.17.15  The  Registrar’s  Environment  shall  process  and  publish  the  final  results  according  to  the  Core
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Calendar.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.17.16  All results shall be recorded and stored on the official mark sheets and electronic database.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: EXAMINATION ENQUIRIES
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.18.1  General
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (a)  The University assumes no responsibility for incorrect information concerning any aspect of
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: the examinations that has been furnished by persons who are not authorised to give such
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: information. All enquiries should be made at Registrar’s Environment.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (b)  All enquiries regarding examination results should be submitted on the prescribed form to
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Registrar’s Environment. within thirty (30) days of the publication of the results.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.18.2  Viewing of examination answering scripts
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (a)  A student may, subject to the payment of the prescribed fee, receive an opportunity to view his
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: or her examination scripts for all theoretical examinations at all levels of all modules/subjects.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Students' Rules and Regulations
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (b)  A student may, subject to the payment of the prescribed fee, apply for a re-checking or re-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: marking after viewing of scripts.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (c)  An  application  for  viewing  of,  or  inspecting  an  examination  script  is  required  to  reach  the
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: Registrar’s Environment  before the published closing date for examination enquiries.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (d)  Memoranda shall not be made available to students during the viewing of scripts process.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.18.3  Re-checking
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (a)  A student may, subject to the payment of the prescribed fee, have his or her examination scripts
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: for all theoretical examinations re-checked at all levels of all modules/subjects.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (b)  A student may, subject to the payment of the prescribed fee, apply for a re-mark after a re-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: check.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: If the student passes the module/subject after re-checking, the fixed fee will be refunded.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (d)  An application for re-checking an examination script is required to the Registrar’s Environment
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: before the published closing date for examination enquiries.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.18.4  Re-marking
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (a)  A student may, subject to the payment of the prescribed fee, have his or her examination
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: scripts for all theoretical examinations re-marked by the moderator at all levels of all modules/
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: subjects. In the event where a student requests a re-mark and the script has been moderated
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: already, the moderator should not conduct the re-mark. The DTLC should assign the task to
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: another qualified person.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: If the student's results change from a "fail" to either "qualify for a supplementary examination"
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: or "pass", or from "pass" to  "pass with distinction", the fixed fee shall be refunded.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (c)  An application for re-marking an examination script is required to reachthe Registrar’s Environ-
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: ment before the published closing date for examination enquiries.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: The right to appeal to examination and related matters
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: If a student is dissatisfied with the outcome of the re-marking, the Registrar’s Environment
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: will refer the student to the DTLC who may appoint another suitably qualified person to do a
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: final re-marking at a set cost.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]
["CHAPTER 4"]

text: If a student submits an appeal regarding alleged examination irregularities, the DTLC shall
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: determine the necessary correctional steps.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: (c)  Memoranda shall not be made available to students during the re-marking or appeal process.
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: 4.1.20  WITHDRAWAL OF RESULTS
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: An examination result, statement or academic report issued erroneously by the University shall not
section_path: ["CHAPTER 4"]

text: be valid and should be returned to the University at its request.

text: TECHNOLOGY, SHAPING THE FUTURE
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: Established  in  2004,  the Tshwane  University  of Technology  (TUT)  is  a  leading
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: African university of technology, offering world-class technology education and
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: applied sciences to more than sixty-thousand students from across South Africa
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: and the African continent.
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: Learning programmes are developed, in collaboration with industry and profes-
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: sional  bodies,  around  specific  cutting-edge  work-related  competencies  and
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: specifications. The primary focus is thus professional and career-focused educa-
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: tion. To promote readiness to practise a career, a system of cooperative educa-
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: tion is in place at the institution, which allows the student to be exposed to a
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: period of learning in the labour market. Academic offerings are also designed
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: with  the  latest  technological  advances  in  mind,  are  student-centred  and  are
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: aimed at the holistic development of each student.
section_path: ["Contents"]

section_path: ["Contents"]

text: Please Note:
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: 1.  Life Orientation and an achievement level of 1 in a subject are not consid-
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: ered in the calculation of the Admission Point Score (APS).
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: 2.  Prospective students will not be admitted to any programme without prior
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: evaluation.
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: 3.  TUT requires a National Senior Certificate (NQF Level 4) or an equivalent
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: qualification, with a minimum of six subjects, including English (home or
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: first additional language with a minimum score of 3), Mathematics (Techni-
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: cal  Mathematics)  or  Mathematical  Literacy  (as  per  specific  academic
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: programme requirement) and the further subjects required by a specific
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: academic programme.
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: BECOME A FUTURE-READY GRADUATE
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: As  a  dynamic  university  of  technology,  the  Tshwane  University  of Technology
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: will  provide  you  with  unlimited  opportunities  for  professional  and  personal
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: development, while equipping you with skills and knowledge to make a positive
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: social  impact. At TUT,  we  value  the  diversity  of  views,  knowledge  and  abili-
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: ties each member of the TUT stakeholder community brings to the University’s
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: quest for excellence in advancing and applying knowledge. Since the University
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: supports progressive thinking and encourages entrepreneurship and innovation,
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: TUT’s seven faculties offer a broad spectrum of widely recognised programmes,
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: many of which are unique to TUT, to choose from. With such a choice, you are
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: bound to find a career just for you! While we excel in the cultural and sporting
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: arena and have a vibrant student life, TUT remains an institution focused on
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: academic excellence. We respond to the needs and challenges of our country
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: and  continent,  thus  new  market-related  courses  are  developed  continuously
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: in close collaboration with trade and industry. In this way, we can ensure that
section_path: ["Contents"]

section_path: ["Contents"]

text: GENERAL INFORMATION
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: To be considered for funding in any academic year, the applicant must ensure
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: to follow due processes and comply with the terms and conditions stipulated
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: and applicable to each funding category. Failing to do so will result in the appli-
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: cation not being considered. As a general rule, no late or incomplete applica-
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: tions will be accepted.
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: The NSFAS website (www.nsfas.org.za) contains future updates in this regard.
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: Students must ensure not to miss the deadline or to wait until the last day.
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: Who should apply?
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: •  Students who are South African citizens.
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: •  Students whose combined family income is less than R350 000 per annum,
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: and in cases of students living with a disability, the combined income is less
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: than R600000 per annum.
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: Please consult the Financial Aid website at www.tut.ac.za/students/financial
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: for updated and relevant information with regard to funding opportunities and
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: application requirements.
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: •  All new applicants (matriculants) or students who passed Grade 12 in previ-
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: ous years, but never registered at any university.
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: •  Students who have never received NSFAS funding.
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: •  If a student applied for, and received funding in any particular year, he or she
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: need to re-apply each year, ensure to visit NSFAS website for clear instruc-
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: tions.  Continued  funding  for  the  subsequent  years  is  based  on  a  student’s
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: academic performance in the year that funding was received.
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: External funding
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: This refers to bursaries that are allocated to students from sources outside of
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: the University. These include undergraduate and postgraduate bursaries from
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: public, private, corporate/industry, government, parastatals and international
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: sources. Please consult our website for more information on possible funding
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: opportunities.
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: •  However, if a student does not register in the subsequent year of funding and
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: has taken a “gap year”, a student will be required to re-apply.

section_path: ["Contents"]

text: NSFAS website to verify their details.
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: Internal University funding
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: Internal awards are allocated to any bona fide student from first-time entering
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: students to postgraduate students who enroll at the University. It is the Univer-
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: sity’s intention to attract  and  retain  quality  students  by rewarding  excellent
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: academic and non-academic performance.
section_path: ["Contents"]

section_path: ["Contents"]

text: Extracurricular Programme:  Peer Education
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: The  directorate  of  Health  and  Wellness  (H&W)  offers  extracurricular  learning
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: and development in the form of the Peer Education Programme. The Peer Educa-
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: tion Programme is a student volunteer-based programme that aim at promoting
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: health and wellbeing among TUT students and surrounding communities.   The
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: programme  is  regarded  as  a  useful  strategy  in  promoting  healthy  living.    The
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: programme empowers students with soft skills that enables them to be devel-
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: oped  holistically  in  support  of  the  academic  skills.    Enrolled  peer  educators
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: assist the Health and Wellness directorate to reach more students and commu-
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: nity members through partnerships formed within other SAED directorates and
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: surrounding communities.  The peer education programme is further utilised as a
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: strategy that promote peer to peer engagements on various life issues.  Various
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: ways in which peer education is utilised by the directorate serve as strengthening
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: strategy that aims at behavioural change among students and supported commu-
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: nities. The programme has evolved into numerous H&W programmes that offer
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: experiential opportunities to enhance leadership, interpersonal, communication
section_path: ["Contents"]

text: and advocacy skills.
section_path: ["Contents"]
